references.text: Earlier warning about having to wander in the wilderness for forty years as punishment for Israel's disobedience and turning away from the Lord.
Moses warns of the consequences of turning away from the Lord—they will die and not live long in the land.
Joshua warns the tribes that turning away from the Lord will bring wrath upon all the congregation of Israel.
Achan's sin affected the entire congregation of Israel, not just himself—showing how one person's sin impacts the whole people.
Judas' falling away and disobedience led to the Lord's wrath and ultimately to destruction without healing.
Warning against an evil and unbelieving heart that falls away from the living God, with reference to Israel's wilderness experience.
The one who turns back has no pleasure in God—falling away leads to perdition.
Those who return to the world after having known salvation find themselves in a worse condition than before.
